title: The Quiet Machine
premise: Marguerite Underhill, a navigator who faked his death twenty years ago to escape the war's conscription archives, discovers his old identity listed on the manifest of the Meridian, a ship officially lost with all hands — including him. The manifest is a message: someone in the Admiralty knows he's alive and is using his 'ghost' status to smuggle peace terms past a war faction that profits from the fighting. Hunted by both sides, Marguerite must choose between erasing himself forever and delivering the transmission that exposes the corruption, knowing it will resurrect the man he buried. He delivers it, ending the war and surrendering his anonymity, but keeps one backup in the hold as insurance against the new peace.
about_author: Sebastian Iversen is a former maritime radio operator from Tromsø who spent a decade aboard Arctic supply vessels before turning to fiction. His work explores how people carry their pasts like cargo, and whether any of us can truly go off the record.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Dead
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Loading cargo at Ceres station, he runs a routine scan and finds his birth name on the Meridian's manifest — a ship that burned nineteen years ago, with him supposedly aboard. He traces the entry to an encrypted Admiralty channel and realizes someone knows. Emotional beat: cold dread as two decades of careful invisibility collapse in a single line of text.

chapters.title: The Hold Full of Sleepers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, intercut with flashbacks to the Meridian's last flight. Pursued by an Admiralty audit vessel, he opens the sealed hold where his own backup sleeps alongside others from the 'lost' crew — evidence someone preserved them deliberately. A boarding officer, Wren Kastel, offers him a choice: run and be erased, or carry the message hidden in the manifest. Emotional beat: vertigo between loyalty to his hidden life and the pull of truth.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Marguerite and Wren. The war faction intercepts them; Wren reveals she's been ordered to kill him once the message transmits, but has begun to doubt her masters. In a running battle through the debris field where the real Meridian died, Marguerite learns the 'loss' was staged to bury the peace terms — and the crew who refused. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve as loyalty shifts from institutions to people.

chapters.title: Last Transmission Loop
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. With Earth's transmission loop closing for another decade, he broadcasts the manifest and the sleepers' testimony fleet-wide, exposing the war profiteers and resurrecting his own name. Wren refuses her kill order and stands witness. The ceasefire holds; Marguerite, no longer invisible, logs his true identity for the first time in twenty years — keeping one backup in the dark. Emotional beat: grief and liberation braided into quiet, hard-won peace.
